what_this_is: The per-world standard error of `revision_held_out`, measured by a cluster bootstrap over withheld transitions rather than over scored cells, for the five design-block cells. It discharges the method the granularity gate now requires; it does not discharge the gate for Stage B.
why_it_exists: docs/STAGE-B-PROTOCOL.md §3.1 and docs/AI-REVIEW-2026-11-03.md finding 3: `score()` returns an aggregate over nested cells, so no per-world standard error existed and `s/sqrt(N)` over the transition count was a substitution.
method: each withheld transition is a cluster; its cells move together because the vocabulary is scored under every transition; the world's score is the ratio (sum of transition losses) / (sum of transition cell counts) and is bootstrapped by resampling transitions with replacement

level_and_reps.reported_quantity: the bootstrap standard deviation of the ratio estimator

cells_are: the consumed calibration seeds, regenerated deterministically; no seed is spent and none is re-allocated
status: method discharged on design-block cells; the gate is NOT confirmed for Stage B, because the bracket straddles the gap
limits: the five seeds are the calibration block, already consumed; they are design-block cells, not the four claimed configurations, so this measures the estimator and does not authorise the run

the two readouts bracket plausible prediction quality (the exact latent rule and the wrong-law control); neither is the organism's readout, whose loss distribution is not available before the run, and a readout with heavier-tailed losses would give a larger standard error
a bootstrap standard deviation is itself estimated: with 2000 replicates per cell its own Monte-Carlo error is a few percent of its value
82 held-out transitions per cell is the count the calibration cells happen to have; the claimed configurations' counts do not exist yet
no_engine: No engine ran and no seed was spent. The worlds are regenerated deterministically from already-consumed seeds to read their withheld sets.
